articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual Auction XXII and swap meet on Sunday, April 28, 2002, at Houge Park, offering a chance to buy and sell astronomical equipment. The document also provides a comprehensive calendar of SJAA activities for April and May 2002, including various astronomy classes, star parties, deep-sky weekends, and general meetings. Details for participation in the auction and swap, along with directions and contact information, are included.

articles.title: Crisium at Lunar Sunset
articles.summary: This article features an observing report by Jane Houston Jones detailing a nighttime session focused on Mare Crisium at lunar sunset, alongside observations of Jupiter and Saturn, utilizing a variety of telescopes and high-quality Zeiss eyepieces. Additionally, it announces several upcoming astronomy-related events, including an SJAA auction, a lecture by Dr. Alex Filippenko on the Big Bang theory, and the annual SJAA Yosemite star party at Glacier Point.

articles.title: Considering Copernicus
articles.summary: This article serves as an enthusiastic observing guide, urging amateur astronomers to explore the prominent lunar crater Copernicus and its rich surrounding features, particularly during April's First Quarter Moon. It provides practical advice on optimal viewing times and magnification, detailing various points of interest including secondary impact craters, rilles like Rima Gay Lussac, nearby craters such as Reinhold, and potential volcanic dome fields. The author emphasizes the dynamic and detailed views available through a telescope, encouraging repeated observations to appreciate the full range of lunar geology.

articles.title: Old Smokey is back on Patrol
articles.summary: The article details the extensive refurbishment of "Old Smokey," an old Celestron 8" SCT from the SJAA loaner program, by Dan Wright and expert Phil Chambers. The telescope, initially in poor condition due to water damage and tracking issues, was meticulously cleaned, repaired, and re-collimated. "Old Smokey" is now fully functional and delivering excellent images, ready for other SJAA members to borrow.

articles.title: Planets in April
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for planets visible in April, highlighting Jupiter's prominent cloud details and moon transits (Europa on the 4th, Io on the 21st). Saturn also offers a spectacular view with its wide-open rings, and observers are encouraged to look for ring details and challenge themselves to distinguish moons from nearby stars. Mercury, Venus, and Mars become visible in the evening sky later in the month, forming a nice grouping, while the outer planets (Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) are late evening or morning objects.

articles.title: AANC Conference May 18, 2002
articles.summary: The AANC Conference, co-sponsored by the College of San Mateo, is scheduled for May 18, 2002. It will feature diverse talks on topics like the Kepler Mission, galactic black holes, and the DART telescope, along with a presentation from Coronado Filters. Attendees can also enjoy solar viewing during lunch, planetarium shows, a spaghetti feed, and a star party after the main presentations.

articles.title: The Red, White, and Blue Star
articles.summary: The article details Iota Orionis, a "red, white, and blue" multiple star system located in Orion's sword, providing guidance on how to observe its distinct colored components with a telescope. It describes the system's various stellar types, including a brilliant O-class primary and fainter companions, and touches upon research into its strong solar winds producing X-rays. An 8-inch telescope is recommended to fully appreciate its colors, and the document also lists upcoming astronomical events.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner telescope program, detailing which scopes are currently available, those on short-term loan, and those with extended loan periods. SJAA members can borrow equipment by contacting Mike Koop, with a waiting list in place for popular items. The list includes various types of telescopes such as Dobsonians, refractors, and a spectroscope.
